item.title: Conduit 0.7.2
item.description:
Improved

  • Searching a conversation highlights each match where it appears, including in code, tool output and raw lines. The match you're on stands out, and ↩ / ⇧↩ (or ⌘G / ⇧⌘G) step one match at a time, scrolling straight to it
  • Search has a match-case toggle (Aa) and works in the raw transcript too, opening the line it lands on
  • Switching between the styled and raw transcript is a Styled · Raw toggle in the search bar and the raw view, beside the toggle for lines Conduit can't render. On the Mac, Session › Show Raw Transcript is ⌥⌘U
  • The MCP connectors list can be filtered, and puts servers that need you first. A server that needs signing in has a button that runs the sign-in in a new terminal tab on the Mac, with Copy command everywhere

Fixed

  • Text in a conversation can be selected across messages, and the transcript scrolls as a selection reaches the top or bottom, so you're no longer limited to what's on screen

item.title: Conduit 0.7.1
item.description:
Improved

  • Database-CLI sources can be marked "Runs psql underneath". Conduit then sends quiet CSV settings with the query, wraps it in a read-only transaction by default, and ignores your own `.psqlrc`
  • Each database-CLI source can set its own environment variables, such as a cloud profile to pick which role it connects as
  • A database-CLI source that fails shows the command's whole output, including sign-in messages it prints to stdout. A command that prints nothing is reported as an error, not as zero rows

Fixed

  • A database-CLI source that takes the SQL as an argument must say where with `{sql}`. Before, the SQL was added to the end of the command, which could run one of the CLI's own subcommands

item.title: Conduit 0.7.0
item.description:
New

  • Dashboards, a new tab on each project: chart your own Postgres, Redshift or database-CLI queries as lines, bars, numbers and tables, set goals on them, and keep notes beside each chart. Open a chart as a tab to edit its SQL, see its history, and run it again
  • Agents can work towards a dashboard goal: chats can query your data sources, add and annotate charts, and hand a goal to an agent they dispatch. Charts they save are drawn right in the transcript
  • Project goals show on the Context tab, and the Activity feed notes when a goal moved after a PR merged
  • A chat waiting on a background task says so above the composer, with its output and a Stop button, instead of looking finished

Improved

  • HTML and Markdown files can be previewed from a diff tab

item.title: Conduit 0.6.0
item.description:
New

  • Conduit Agent, an early preview: a third agent beside Claude Code and Codex that runs open models on Amazon Bedrock with your own AWS account, no other CLI needed. Set it up from a server's profile (Conduit Agent provider…) with this machine's AWS sign-in or a Bedrock API key, then pick it as a chat's agent. It reads, edits and searches files, runs commands, asks before acting, plans, and can dispatch and work alongside project agents
  • An emoji button in the Mac's composers opens the system emoji picker
  • Script output can be selected and copied

Improved

  • The Git tab is an outline of the workspace's work: its PRs and how they stack, what isn't on a PR yet, and each branch's commits and files in place
  • A branch is diffed against its PR's base, so a review shows only what that PR adds
  • New worktree chats start from the same composer on the Mac and on phones, and phones can paste attachments into the first message
  • A worktree being created already looks like the workspace it becomes
  • ⌘R runs the dev server from any pane, and new worktrees no longer start it unless you tick the box
  • Grok models are no longer offered or run, with any agent

Fixed

  • Agents a chat dispatches could start signed out when Claude's sign-in comes from your shell profile
  • A dispatched agent that crashes, fails its setup, runs out of runs for the day or stops without reporting now tells the chat that dispatched it
  • Mark as Unread on the chat in view sticks on the Mac

item.title: Conduit 0.5.0
item.description:
New

  • A new worktree's pane opens the moment you press Start, with your first message waiting in it while git makes the worktree
  • Folder and project headers in the sidebar count their unread chats

Improved

  • Unread chats stand out, and a chat is marked read only once you've seen it, including after a relaunch
  • Long transcripts scroll smoothly: messages you've already scrolled past aren't rebuilt
  • Opening an earlier session while its worktree's chat is running shows it straight away, beside the running chat
  • On the Mac, Add workspace in a project opens the New Worktree dialog with the project chosen, and opens the new worktree
  • Typing in the composer leaves the transcript where you scrolled it, so you can quote earlier parts

Fixed

  • A chat you come back to while it's working stays live however long the run takes, rather than folding its work and unlocking mid-run
  • Scripts that finished quickly no longer show as running, and old failures don't come back on every launch
  • Clicking an earlier session under a busy worktree no longer does nothing
  • Opening a session from a folder pane no longer covers the pane with a full-screen chat
  • A failed worktree creation is reported instead of passing for success
  • A failed conduit.json read no longer passes for a missing file
  • Cancelling a Claude sign-in waits for the login to exit

item.title: Conduit 0.4.0
item.description:
New

  • A Reviews tab in each folder shows the PRs waiting on your review, your re-review, or someone else's, oldest wait first
  • Line notes on a PR's diff can go to GitHub as a pending review, submitted as Comment, Approve or Request changes
  • Reply to and resolve a PR's review threads from the diff or the review chip
  • Tick off reviewed files, synced with GitHub's Viewed boxes, and re-review only what came after your last look
  • PR rows show their checks, conflicts, unresolved threads and requested reviewers
  • On phones, the home shows chats that need you and those running, and searches every folder
  • Android keeps a backgrounded run alive and notifies like the Mac, and other apps can share text and files to a chat
  • On the Mac, the chat's composer stays docked under files and diffs, so comments join it as you write them

Improved

  • A stacked branch's diff shows only what its own PR adds, against the rung below it
  • Diffs expand the unchanged lines around each hunk, as on GitHub
  • Typing ``` closes the code block, in the composer and in Markdown files
  • Agents can be dispatched into a repo the project has no workspace in yet
  • A folder's dev server is pinned in every worktree's Scripts
  • Phones start a chat from a sheet before making its worktree, with visible tabs and an attach button
  • Phones get the desktop's session actions, file breadcrumbs, pull to refresh, and Find in the file viewer
  • Android: predictive back, edge to edge, and a branded launch screen and themed icon
  • The sidebar, menus and workspace panes redraw only what a change touches, so many open chats stay smooth

Fixed

  • Chat attachments and Conduit's worktrees no longer show up as git changes
  • Back from unsaved edits in a phone file asks before discarding them
  • A server's saved password is kept until its removal is confirmed
  • A connection dropped mid-command no longer leaves a folder's sessions loading for good
  • Commenting on a diff no longer blocks the buttons that expand its hidden lines

item.title: Conduit 0.3.0
item.description:
Improved

  • Bold, italic, code and links are styled as you type in every field whose text goes to Claude: line comments, question answers, the new-worktree prompt and feedback
  • Script output shows in the inspector's Scripts tab
  • Long chats open at the bottom straight away, and reopen without re-reading the whole transcript
  • Commands on This Mac start much faster: they no longer source your shell profile each time
  • Big repos stay quick: the palette and branch lists, a worktree's changes, and pull request and workspace reads all cost far less
  • Chats no longer recompute their status chips on every streamed word
  • Long diffs, files and project activity build only the rows on screen, and big edits no longer stall the chat
  • Hidden chats, the sidebar and streaming replies redraw far less, so many open chats stay smooth
  • Refreshing, refocusing the window and following a run ask the host much less, and never pile up on a slow one
  • Script output is capped so long runs stay responsive, and image thumbnails are decoded at the size they're shown

item.title: Conduit 0.2.1
item.description:
Improved

  • Codex chats taken over from Claude Code show their tool calls as steps, not raw tags, and drop Conductor's instructions from titles and prompts
  • Codex chats name Codex in the transcript and the composer
  • Fenced code in the composer is drawn as one panel
  • Whole PR stacks are found in busy repos, and drawn like GitHub's

Fixed

  • Sending comments from a diff tab with Ask Claude no longer leaves the chat blank

item.title: Conduit 0.2.0
item.description:
New

  • Sign in to GitHub through Conduit's GitHub App, and choose which repositories it can see
  • A branch's GitHub review shows in its diffs, and as a review chip in the chat
  • A welcome pane walks a new Mac user through an agent, GitHub and a first folder
  • Send feedback or report a bug from the Help menu, filed as a public GitHub issue

Improved

  • Folder settings live in the folder's conduit.json, so they reach every worktree
  • The project brief's text can be selected
  • The conduit.json schema is served from the public releases repo

item.title: Conduit 0.1.4
item.description:
Improved

  • The project brief takes the Context tab's full width
  • Open pull requests moved into the activity feed, as an Open PRs filter

item.title: Conduit 0.1.3
item.description:
New

  • Conduit now updates itself: Conduit › Check for Updates…, and a daily check
  • Import your worktrees and chats from Conductor
  • An MCP status chip next to the context ring, for Claude and Codex chats
  • HTML files open as tabs with a preview and Open in Browser
  • Copy buttons on code blocks in Claude's messages
  • Edit the project brief in place on desktop
  • Folder settings open as a tab in the pane
  • A teardown script can run when a worktree is archived
  • A server profile can name its Codex executable

Improved

  • The desktop composer is now a single rounded Mac message field
  • The project pane gains Context and Workspaces tabs, with activity as a column
  • Signing in to GitHub is built in, and tokens renew themselves
  • Codex reads newer rollouts
  • In the palette, a pull request opens its worktree
